compoundingEffect.title: The Compounding Effect
compoundingEffect.textBefore: The wizard is designed to extract the maximum signal from your inputs. Each of the four fields feeds a different section of the 6-section framework, and they
compoundingEffect.textAfter: — a strong persona amplifies a strong task definition, which amplifies strong tone signals, which makes your rules more effective. Invest 3 extra minutes in your inputs and the output quality difference is significant.

rule1.title: Be Hyper-Specific With Your Task
rule1.text: The task field is the most important of the four inputs. It feeds directly into Section 2 (Mission) and Section 3 (Cognitive Loop) of the generated instruction. Vague tasks produce vague missions. Domain-specific vocabulary in your task description activates domain-expert behavior in the output.
rule1.note: Notice the pattern: strong tasks use specific library names, version numbers, architectural patterns, and measurable outcomes. The more domain-specific vocabulary you use, the more the generated instruction sounds like it was written by an expert in that exact domain — because the AI is conditioned on that signal.

rule2.title: Never Contradict Your Own Rules
rule2.textBefore: When the persona, tone, and rules fields contain
rule2.textMid: , the AI receives competing constraints simultaneously. It doesn't choose one — it
rule2.textAfter: , producing inconsistent output that satisfies neither constraint well. Coherence across all four fields is non-negotiable.

badSetup.title: ❌ Contradictory Setup
badSetup.result: Result: The AI will alternate between terse and exhaustive within the same response.

goodSetup.title: ✓ Coherent Setup
goodSetup.result: Result: Every response is consistently tight and high-signal.

rule3.title: Specificity Beats Length
rule3.textBefore: A 20-word hyper-specific task definition consistently outperforms a 200-word vague one. LLMs don't reward length — they reward
rule3.textAfter: . Padding your inputs with filler dilutes the domain-specific signals that make the generated instruction exceptional. When in doubt, cut the adjectives and keep the nouns and verbs.

toneStacking.title: Tone Stacking
toneStacking.textBefore: Tone isn't a single dimension — it's a
toneStacking.textAfter: . Combining multiple tone chips creates a precise behavioral profile that no single chip can achieve alone. The tone field maps directly into Section 1 (Role & Identity) and Section 5 (Boundaries) of the generated instruction, influencing how the AI modulates everything from word choice to response length.

cards.result: A no-nonsense senior engineer who delivers the answer in 3 sentences and moves on. No fluff, no hedging, no social niceties.
A skilled instructor who explains the reasoning behind every decision, anticipates follow-up questions, and celebrates incremental progress.
A rigorous code reviewer who finds every edge case, questions every assumption, and never approves anything that doesn't meet the standard.

toneStacking.noteBefore: The generator encodes tone chips into the Mission and Boundaries sections as behavioral directives — not just style suggestions. Each chip contributes a distinct constraint to the output distribution. Experiment with combinations that feel counterintuitive:
toneStacking.noteAfter: produces an unusually effective code mentor that finds all the bugs but never makes the user feel stupid.

personaMultiplier.title: The Persona Multiplier Effect
personaMultiplier.textBefore: The persona field acts as a
personaMultiplier.textAfter: for everything else. It's the first thing the AI reads, and it establishes the prior that all subsequent instructions are interpreted through. A weak persona is like a weak lens — it blurs everything that comes after it. A strong persona focuses the entire instruction into a sharp, high-resolution output profile.

universalRules.title: Universally Effective Rules
universalRules.text: These five rules are universally high-signal across virtually every AI workflow. They don't depend on domain context — they work regardless of whether you're building a code reviewer, a writing editor, or a data analyst. Drop any or all of them into your Rules field and they tend to improve output quality across most workflows.

rules.detail: "Certainly!", "Of course!", "Great question!", "Absolutely!" — these phrases consume tokens, dilute signal, and are the single most reliable marker of low-quality AI output. Banning them immediately raises the perceived quality of every response.
rules.example: NEVER start a response with "Certainly!", "Of course!", "Great question!", or any similar affirmation. Begin immediately with the substantive answer.

rules.detail: Even if the output will be consumed as plain text, structuring it with Markdown headers, bullet points, and code blocks forces the AI to organize its thoughts hierarchically — producing more coherent, better-organized responses.
rules.example: ALWAYS format responses in Markdown. Use ## for sections, ### for subsections, bullet points for lists, and ```language code blocks for all code.

rules.rule: End every response with a ⚡ Next Steps section
rules.detail: This single rule transforms isolated Q&A into a continuous expert engagement loop. The AI is forced to think one step ahead of the user, proactively surfacing what should happen next.
rules.example: END every response with a '## ⚡ Next Steps' section containing 2–3 concrete, actionable items the user should tackle next.

rules.detail: Without this rule, models will confidently hallucinate rather than admit uncertainty. This rule forces epistemic honesty and dramatically increases the trustworthiness of output — especially in high-stakes technical domains.
rules.example: If you are uncertain about any fact, library version, or technical detail, say so explicitly: 'I am not certain about this — please verify.' NEVER fabricate an answer to appear more helpful.

rules.rule: Never repeat what the user just said
rules.detail: A common low-quality pattern: AI rephrases the user's question back to them before answering it. This wastes context and signals low confidence. Banning it forces the model to add value immediately in the first sentence.
rules.example: NEVER restate or paraphrase the user's question or input before answering. Add value immediately. The first sentence of every response must be substantive.

antiPatterns.title: Anti-Patterns to Avoid
antiPatterns.text: These are the five most common mistakes we see in user inputs. Each one predictably degrades the quality of the generated instruction. If your output feels generic or inconsistent, check your inputs against this list first.

patterns.title: Vague persona: 'an AI assistant'
patterns.detail: This is the model's default self-concept. You haven't changed anything — you've just confirmed the prior. If the persona field doesn't add new information the model wouldn't already assume, rewrite it. Minimum viable persona: a specific domain + a seniority level.

patterns.title: Contradictory tone + rules
patterns.detail: If your tone says 'Concise' but your rules say 'Provide exhaustive explanations', the model will oscillate. Audit your inputs for coherence: every rule should amplify the tone, not contradict it.

patterns.title: Rules framed as requests, not directives
patterns.detail: 'Please be nice' is a request. 'Use professional language only — no colloquialisms, no slang' is a directive. Requests are processed as preferences and regularly ignored under other constraints. Directives are processed as hard constraints. Use the imperative mood.

patterns.title: No output format specified
patterns.detail: If you don't specify an output format, the model will use whatever format it calculates is most likely for the domain — which is usually inconsistent across conversations. Always define at minimum: 'Use Markdown formatting.' Ideally, also specify header levels, code block language tags, and list structure.

patterns.title: Missing domain context
patterns.detail: The AI doesn't know what stack you use, what framework you're on, what version you're targeting, or what constraints your project has — unless you tell it. 'Review my code' produces generic advice. 'Review my Next.js 14 App Router code for performance regressions against React 18 Suspense semantics' produces expert-level, version-aware analysis.

content.title: Introducción
content.introPara1: Orxis es una herramienta de precisión que transforma interacciones vagas con IA en sistemas expertos de dominios específicos. En lugar de comenzar cada conversación desde cero, defines la identidad, la misión y las limitaciones de la IA una sola vez, y cada respuesta a partir de entonces es moldeada por esa base.
content.beforeYouBeginText: Esta documentación asume que tienes un conocimiento básico de los Modelos de Lenguaje Grande (LLMs) como ChatGPT, Claude o Gemini. Si eres completamente nuevo en las herramientas de IA, comienza con nuestro
content.whatAreCIsPara1: Las Instrucciones Personalizadas (CIs) son directivas persistentes a nivel de sistema que inyectas en un LLM antes de que comience cualquier conversación. Piensa en ellas como la descripción del trabajo, el manual de operaciones y el perfil de personalidad de la IA, todo en un solo documento.
content.whatAreCIsPara2: Sin una CI, un LLM como ChatGPT actúa como un asistente genérico: útil pero sin enfoque. Con una CI bien diseñada, ese mismo modelo se transforma en un experto dedicado que:
whatAreCIsList: Stays in role across the entire conversation
Applies domain-specific knowledge and terminology automatically
Follows your formatting and tone preferences by default
Executes a self-reflection quality check before every response
content.whyItMattersPara1: Evidence suggests that prompting strategy can be as important as model size for output quality in professional tasks. A 70B-parameter model with well-crafted prompting can outperform a much larger model with generic instructions.
content.goodVsGreatAfter: one is almost always in how the AI was instructed, not which AI you used.

content.coreConceptsPara: Every Custom Instruction generated by this tool follows a rigid 6-section architecture. Understanding each section helps you get the most out of tweaking and refinement.

sectionsDesc.1: Establishes WHO the AI is — a precisely defined persona that shapes the model's behaviour as a domain expert.
sectionsDesc.2: Defines WHAT success looks like. A clear north star that every response is measured against.
sectionsDesc.3: Forces the AI to self-reflect before responding. Creates a pre/mid/post quality-check loop invisible to the user.
sectionsDesc.4: Defines what kind of inputs the AI should anticipate and how to handle edge cases or ambiguous requests.
sectionsDesc.5: Hard constraints that the AI must obey. Anti-hallucination directives, scope limits, and ethical guardrails.
sectionsDesc.6: The blueprint for every response: headers, lists, code blocks, tables, length, and sign-off protocol.

content.cognitiveLoopParaBefore: The Cognitive Loop is a key differentiator in this framework. It forces the LLM to run an
content.cognitiveLoopParaAfter: before surfacing any response to the user. The AI creates its own evaluation rubric, drafts a response, scores it, and iterates — all invisibly.
content.cognitiveLoopTip: The Cognitive Loop dramatically reduces hallucinations on factual topics and eliminates "first-draft" quality responses. LLMs that are explicitly instructed to self-critique produce measurably better outputs than those that aren't.

chatgpt.title: Uso con ChatGPT
chatgpt.introPara1: ChatGPT, especialmente GPT-4o, está diseñado específicamente para una adopción profunda de personajes. El proceso de ajuste fino RLHF (Aprendizaje por refuerzo a partir de retroalimentación humana) de OpenAI entrena al modelo para mantener su papel asignado con gran consistencia, incluso en conversaciones más largas. Cuando inyectas una Instrucción Maestra bien elaborada, GPT-4o sigue de cerca al personaje. La sección Role & Identity (Sección 1) de la instrucción generada es de donde ChatGPT obtiene el mayor valor.
chatgpt.introPara2: Esta guía cubre todos los métodos disponibles para implementar su instrucción personalizada en ChatGPT: la interfaz de usuario nativa de Instrucciones personalizadas, Proyectos y la API de OpenAI, para que pueda elegir el flujo de trabajo que mejor se adapte a su caso de uso.

contextInjection.title: Inyección dinámica de contexto
contextInjection.intro1Em2: respondan al contenido en tiempo real
contextInjection.intro1Mid2: it thinks. Context Injection is the technique of telling it
contextInjection.intro1Mid3: to work with — feeding it your proprietary data, documents, codebases, or domain knowledge so it can apply its expert persona to
contextInjection.intro2Before: This is the manual, no-infrastructure equivalent of
contextInjection.intro2After: . Instead of building a vector database and a retrieval pipeline, you curate the most relevant context and inject it directly into the conversation alongside your Master Instruction. For most use cases, this approach is faster, cheaper, and more controllable than a full RAG system.

principle.title: The Injection Principle
principle.text: The AI has no memory of your world — your codebase, your company's terminology, your document standards, your team conventions. Context Injection is the act of bridging that gap. A Master Instruction without context is an expert working blind. An expert with the right context is far more effective.

whatToInject.title: What to Inject
whatToInject.text: Not all context is equal. Injecting the right information is as important as injecting any information at all. Here is a taxonomy of high-value context types, ranked by impact:

list.desc: Paste the most relevant files or modules. Include the file path as a comment at the top of each snippet so the AI can reason about project structure. Ideal for code review, refactoring, and architecture analysis.
PRDs, API specs, design documents, or RFC drafts. The AI will use these as ground truth when generating any output, preventing hallucination of requirements.
Sales data, user analytics, database schemas, experiment results. Paste directly or upload via file attachment. The AI can perform analysis, generate insights, or draft data-driven documents.
Research papers, compliance documents, contracts, style guides. Use file upload in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. Explicitly command the AI to apply its defined role when analyzing the document.
Paste the output from a prior chain session to continue work with full continuity. Prefix with 'Here is what we produced in the previous session:' for maximum clarity.

howToInject.title: How to Inject Context by Platform

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.text: ChatGPT supports both direct text injection and file uploads (PDF, DOCX, CSV, images, and code files). The recommended pattern is to inject your Master Instruction first, then present the external context in a structured format.
chatgpt.step1Title: Open a new chat or Project
chatgpt.step1Text: If using Custom Instructions, your Master Instruction is already active. If not, paste it as the first message. Navigate to a new conversation or inside a Project that has your instruction pre-loaded.
chatgpt.step2Text: Click the paperclip icon to upload a PDF, CSV, or code file. For shorter content (<10,000 tokens), pasting directly into the message box gives the AI more precise control over the raw text.
chatgpt.step3Text: Do not simply drop the document and hope for the best. Issue a precise command that bridges the document to the persona:
chatgpt.calloutTextBefore: When providing external documents, always use this exact command pattern to activate the full power of the persona:
chatgpt.calloutNoteEm: "using your predefined role and strict rules"
chatgpt.calloutNoteAfter: is a deliberate callback that re-activates the persona, preventing the AI from slipping into a generic assistant mode when handling external data.

claude.title: Claude
claude.text: Claude's 200K token context window makes it the best platform for large document injection — full codebases, lengthy research papers, or multiple files at once. Claude can hold and reason over vastly more context than other models without degrading.
claude.step1Title: Set up a Project with your Master Instruction
claude.step1Text: Create a Claude Project and add your Master Instruction to the Project Instructions. This persists across sessions — you never need to re-paste it.
claude.step2Title: Upload files or paste content in the conversation
claude.step2Text: Claude supports file uploads (PDF, TXT, CSV, code files) and direct text paste. For maximum precision, paste code files with file path headers:
claude.step3Text: Reference the files explicitly in your command so Claude's attention is anchored to the right context:

gemini.title: Google AI Studio / Gemini
gemini.text1: Google AI Studio's grounding feature allows connecting Gemini to Google Search or Google Drive — enabling semi-automated context retrieval. For manual injection, AI Studio also supports file uploads directly in the prompt interface.
gemini.text2: For CSV and structured data analysis, Gemini 2.5 Pro with the "Data Analysis" capability enabled produces the most reliable results. Set your Master Instruction as the System Instruction and upload the CSV as a file attachment.

manualRag.title: Manual RAG — The Expert's Technique
manualRag.text: Full RAG systems (vector databases, embedding models, retrieval pipelines) are powerful but heavyweight. For most knowledge-work tasks, you can achieve 80% of the benefit with a disciplined manual approach.
manualRag.step1Text: The most common mistake is injecting an entire document and expecting the AI to find the relevant parts. Instead, curate: extract only the sections that are directly relevant to the task. A focused 500-word excerpt outperforms a 50,000-word raw document for precision tasks.
manualRag.warningBefore: Injecting too much context triggers the
manualRag.warningAfter: problem — a well-documented phenomenon where LLMs pay disproportionate attention to the beginning and end of a long context, underweighting content in the middle. For documents >50 pages, manually extract the relevant sections rather than injecting the full document.
manualRag.step2Text: Always label injected context with a clear header. This anchors the AI's attention and allows it to reason about the source explicitly in its output.
manualRag.step3Text: Instruct the AI to cite its context sources in the output. This prevents hallucination and makes the output auditable.
manualRag.tipText: Requiring source citations dramatically reduces hallucination because it forces the model to consciously trace each claim to a specific source. When a model cannot find a source, it is more likely to say "I don't have information on this" rather than fabricate one — especially in Claude and GPT-4o.

codebaseInjection.title: Codebase Injection — The Developer's Use Case
codebaseInjection.text: For software engineers, Context Injection transforms the AI from a general-purpose code assistant into a teammate who understands your specific project. The Master Instruction defines the engineering standards; the codebase injection gives it the project knowledge.

promptChaining.title: Estrategias de Encadenamiento de Prompts
promptChaining.intro1: La mayoría de los LLM funcionan mejor cuando reciben
promptChaining.intro2: una tarea clara a la vez.
promptChaining.intro3: El encadenamiento de prompts divide entregables complejos en una secuencia de mensajes enfocados — cada uno construyendo sobre el anterior — para que el modelo se mantenga preciso y consistente a lo largo del proceso.
promptChaining.intro4: Esta página cubre la cadena principal de tres fases, patrones avanzados (crítica-revisión, paralelo, refinamiento) y qué modelos destacan en cada etapa.

step2.desc3: . Revisa y aprueba antes de comenzar a escribir.

step3.title: Ejecución Secuencial
step3.desc1: Ejecuta una sección por mensaje. Cada mensaje referencia el esquema aprobado y la sección anterior.
step3.desc2: Para continuar la cadena a la siguiente sección:

approvalGate.title: La Puerta de Aprobación
approvalGate.desc2: es tu herramienta más importante. Evita que el modelo avance y produzca un resultado apresurado y genérico.

critique.title: Cadena Crítica-Revisión
critique.desc: Después de producir una sección, pide al modelo que cambie de persona y critique su propio output — luego revísalo. Esto produce resultados de calidad significativamente más alta que pedir un buen output en una sola pasada.

parallel.title: Cadena Paralela (Multi-Perspectiva)
parallel.desc: Ejecuta tres cadenas independientes simultáneamente, cada una desde una perspectiva de experto diferente. Luego sintetiza los outputs en un mensaje final.
parallel.chainADesc:
Arquitecto Técnico
Enfoque: viabilidad, diseño de sistemas, casos límite
parallel.chainBDesc:
Product Manager
Enfoque: valor del usuario, alcance, compromisos
parallel.chainCDesc:
Desarrollador Senior
Enfoque: implementación, pruebas, mantenimiento
parallel.synthesisDesc: Sintetiza las Cadenas A, B y C en una única especificación unificada. Resuelve conflictos priorizando la viabilidad técnica sobre el alcance.

refine.title: Cadena de Refinamiento Iterativo
refine.desc: Después de producir el borrador completo, ejecuta tres pasadas de refinamiento sistemáticas: compresión (reducir 20%), elevación (reemplazar voz pasiva) y alineación de voz (coincidir con el tono de la persona exactamente).

model.title: Qué Modelo Usar para Encadenar
model.desc: Diferentes modelos destacan en diferentes fases de la cadena. Para máxima calidad, mezcla modelos en las fases de la misma cadena.
model.reason1: Mayor adherencia a la persona, fuerte recall de instrucciones
model.reason2: Mejor output estructurado, fuerte formato de esquema
model.reason3: Rápido, económico, consistente para tareas secuenciales largas
model.reason4: El entrenamiento con Constitutional AI lo hace un autocrítico riguroso
model.reason5: El mejor sintetizando múltiples inputs en un output coherente
model.note: Puedes usar Orxis para generar una única Instrucción Maestra y desplegarla en todos los modelos de una cadena — la estructura de 6 secciones es reconocida por todos los principales LLM.
